Earnings call transcript: PepsiCo Q3 2026

Published 2026-10-06 03:15 UTC

PepsiCo held its third-quarter 2026 earnings call on Tuesday, with executives discussing results that showed modest organic revenue growth as price increases slowed and volumes in North American snacks remained under pressure. The following is an edited summary of the main points from the prepared remarks and the question-and-answer session with analysts.

The chief executive said organic revenue rose 2.5% in the quarter, driven by international markets, where beverage volumes grew in Latin America and parts of Asia. In North America, snack volumes declined 2% as shoppers traded down to cheaper store brands and bought smaller packages. The company has responded with more promotions and lower-priced pack sizes.

The chief financial officer said gross margin improved slightly thanks to productivity programs and easing costs for packaging and freight. The company reaffirmed its full-year forecast for low-single-digit organic revenue growth and said core earnings per share would rise about 6% in constant currency.

Analysts asked about the impact of weight-loss drugs on snack demand. Executives said they have seen a small effect among households using the medications and are developing smaller portions, higher-protein products and more beverages with less sugar. They said the trend is one of several shifts in eating habits that the portfolio will need to address.

Another analyst asked about marketing spending. The company plans to increase advertising in the fourth quarter around major sporting events and the holiday season, focusing on its largest brands. Executives also discussed plans to simplify the product lineup by removing slower-selling flavors.

On capital returns, the company said it remains on track to pay about $7.6 billion in dividends this year and to continue modest share buybacks. Executives closed by saying they expect volume trends in North America to improve gradually next year as pricing becomes more competitive.
